newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on speculation, rates.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on speculation, rates.

text.p: Secondary money market rates closed up across the board but off session highs on Thursday due to pressure from U.S. long-term interest rates and speculation by a big market player, traders said.
Overnight Cetes rates reined in earlier gains to close up 40 basis points at 27.30 percent, compared to a session high of 28.50 percent.
"A big player held on to its money until late, and began to play around with the market and put rates under considerable pressure," said a trader.
Once rates were high enough, (the player) began to buy paper. The market closed liquid," he added.
Other traders said Mexican secondary rates were under pressure from a rise in U.S. long-bond rates.
"Although it was not the main reason, higher U.S. long-bond rates did influence both the money and the foreign exchange markets," said a trader.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield stood at 6.49 percent as the Mexican money market closed, up from a recent low of 6.32 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile matched developments on government paper, closing up 75 basis points at 28.75 percent, but off session highs of 29.50 percent.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 7.279 billion pesos to offset liquidity shortages by auctioning four credits which it assigned at rates of between 28.90 and 29.13 percent.
Total credit maturities for Friday are 9.315 billion pesos, nonetheless government spending of some four billion pesos is expected to ease liquidity shortfalls.
